title: A novel method for utilizing dichoptic attention tasks in amblyopic training
author: Hou

steps.title: Set up stereoscope and monitors
steps.instruction: Align the left‑eye and right‑eye views using an adjustable mirror stereoscope; adjust horizontal and vertical deviations so that the nonius lines are perfectly aligned under the participant's best optical correction; seat the participant 85 cm from a pair of Sony Trinitron Multiscan G400 CRT monitors running at 85 Hz; ensure both monitors present identical images to the two eyes.

substeps.instruction: Place the mirror stereoscope in front of the participant.
Adjust the mirrors until the nonius lines coincide.
Position the CRT monitors at a viewing distance of 85 cm.
Verify the monitors are set to a frame rate of 85 Hz.

steps.title: Configure stimulus contrast and Gabors
steps.instruction: Set Gabor patch contrast to 35 % in each eye (≥ 25 % contrast, 2 cycles/deg spatial frequency); present vertical Gabors (targets) only to the amblyopic (trained) eye and horizontal Gabors (distractors) only to the fellow (untrained) eye; each trial contains 4 vertical targets and 3 horizontal distractors (total 7 patches).

steps.title: Program trial sequence and timing
steps.instruction: Program each trial to start with a central fixation point and aligned nonius lines; after fixation, display a 500 ms valid cue (square) indicating which eye will receive the targets; then present the random Gabor array for a duration that follows the training stage (initially 1000 ms, decreasing progressively to 200 ms); follow the array with a 200 ms noise mask; allow participants to self‑initiate the next trial and respond as accurately as possible with no time limit and no feedback.

substeps.instruction: Present 500 ms cue square (valid for the trained eye).
Display Gabor array for 200–1000 ms depending on session stage.
Wait for participant response; record accuracy; no feedback is given.

steps.title: Implement cueing proportion
steps.instruction: Within each block, randomize trial order so that 90 % of trials cue the amblyopic eye and 10 % cue the fellow eye.

steps.title: Conduct training schedule
steps.instruction: Have participants attend the lab twice per week, each visit lasting about 2 hours, for a total of 2 months (≈16 visits); aim for roughly 7000 trials across all visits; progressively decrease stimulus display duration from 1000 ms to 200 ms across sessions.
